label: rejected

evidence.V1: Top view reads clearly as a plank floor, but front/three-quarter/silhouette read as a plain 2-stud-deep box with tiny bumps on top (a crate/plinth rather than a floor).
evidence.V2: Medium planks and small nail dots exist, but the big mass is an unarticulated deep base block that takes over half the read; only 4 nails on 9 planks.
evidence.V3: Chunky planks are pleasantly stylised, but the tall slab base under them is a stiff primitive and makes the floor piece read thick and boxy.
evidence.V4: Planks have consistent chamfers that catch light (edge close-up), but the base box edges look near-razor with no visible bevel - inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Close-ups (studio and flat) clean: no pinches, seams or z-fighting; gap lines between planks crisp. Gates A17/A18 pass, 0 flipped faces.
evidence.V6: One wood hue in ~3 values (light, mid, dark base) plus ink nails; colourways (walnut, teal) hold the same disciplined value structure.
evidence.V7: 396 tris vs module target 800 - well under.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor white material, wood hue as specified for plank floors, but unchamfered base box breaks the kit's chamfered-edge rule.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct for a modular piece: Anchored, Box collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic; T1 tiling passes with IoU 1.0 on X and Y.

evidence.V1: Top view reads as planks, but the 4x4x2 block silhouette and three-quarter read as a wooden crate/box rather than a floor.
evidence.V2: Base block (big), planks in two values (medium), nails (small), though nails appear only on two planks.
evidence.V3: Planks are short and chunky (few, brick-like boards) on a tall plain base, so it reads more like paving or a box than floorboards.
evidence.V4: Consistent chamfers on plank edges visible in the planks and edge close-ups.
evidence.V5: Close-ups clean; no seams, pinches or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Oak in three values plus ink nails; colourways disciplined.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, wood hue, chamfers, ink nails: kit-consistent.
evidence.V9: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Box, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 pass both axes.

evidence.V1: Top view reads clearly as a plank floor, but front and silhouette show only a plain 4x4x2 box with a slightly overhanging ridged lid, which reads as a crate/block rather than flooring at 64 px.
evidence.V2: Big (base block) and medium (staggered planks in 3 values) are clear; small detail is sparse: ink nail heads appear on only two of the eight planks and the deep base sides are blank.
evidence.V3: Plank tops have a slight stylised overhang and chunky thickness, but the deep untextured base and evenly sized boards read as stiff primitives.
evidence.V4: Close_planks studio shows consistent chamfers on every plank edge and end catching a highlight; base block edges carry a smaller but even bevel.
evidence.V5: Studio and flat close-ups are clean: flat plank tops, no pinches, seams, z-fighting or stray faceting; A17/A18 pass.
evidence.V6: One wood hue in three values (light, mid, dark planks) plus a darker base and ink nails; walnut and teal colourways keep the same structure.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, wood hue for a plank floor per wave-2 spec, kit-range chamfers, ink iron nails; consistent with the kit anchor look.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Box collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart white + SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 tiling passes on X and Y (iou 1.0).

artifacts: planks overhang the base box slightly, leaving a visible lip/step around the top rim in front view (designed, but reads like a lid on a box)
top_fixes: Reduce the base depth or break it up (joists/beams, darker recessed underside) so the piece reads as a floor, not a crate
Add 0.05-0.07 stud chamfers to the base box edges to match the planks and kit
Make the plank layout more regular (consistent running bond) and add nails to more planks for small-scale detail
Use longer, narrower boards running the full module length with staggered butt joints so it reads as floorboards
Put nail pairs at every board end (or none) for consistent small detail
Darken or recess the base sides (or add a joist line) so the piece stops reading as a crate
Give the base sides a joist/beam read (visible joist ends or a darker beam band) or make the slab thinner so the side view reads as flooring, not a box
Add nails consistently to every plank (two per board end) for even small-scale detail
Vary plank widths or add slight end-grain/board-end splits for more stylised character
